title: Exam Week
subtitle: Ten weeks of grammar and one very determined knight. One paper for both.
objectives: Recall the ten English topics of the term
Use the delete-it test on a pronoun
Find the subject before choosing the verb
Recall the episodes of Don Quixote covered this term

cards.title: Two strands, one paper
cards.text: Nouns, pronouns, tense and agreement on one side. Don Quixote on the other. Both are examinable.

cards.title: Ten weeks, one tap each
cards.text: This is your revision sheet. The second line of each is the mistake that costs the mark.

cards.title: One rule settles most of the marks
cards.text: An apostrophe never makes a plural. It marks possession, or a letter that has been removed.
points: **Expand it.** If 'it is' fits, use it's.

question.explain: Expand it: 'the horse lost it is shoe' is nonsense, so it takes no apostrophe.

cards.title: The delete-it test takes two seconds
cards.text: For any -self word, take it out and read the sentence again. If it still works, it was only emphasis.
points: **'I did it myself'** still works without it.

cards.title: Find the subject, then ignore everything else
cards.text: The verb agrees with the subject. Exam questions bury the subject behind a phrase on purpose.
points: **'The box of nails is heavy.'** Box is the subject.
**In there is and there are**, there is never the subject.

options: The list of names is on the desk.
The list of names are on the desk.
The list of names were on the desk.
The list of names have been on the desk.
question.explain: The subject is list, not names. Cross out the phrase between them and it becomes obvious.

cards.title: Good place to pause
cards.text: Part 2 is the novel and exam technique. The paper after it is 24 questions.

cards.title: One idea runs through every chapter
cards.text: He decides what things mean before he looks at them, and nothing that happens afterwards can change it.

cards.title: The enchanter explains away everything
cards.text: From the library onwards, whenever the world disagrees with him, a wizard did it. It is an argument nothing can beat.
points: **A flock of sheep** is two armies.

cards.title: An unbeatable explanation is a warning sign
cards.text: If nothing could ever prove an idea wrong, that is not its strength. It is the problem with it.
points: **It is what keeps the book going.**
**Ask of any claim:** what would disprove this?
**No answer means** it is not really a claim.

cards.title: Retell means what happened, in order
cards.text: Name who, where and what changed. Do not judge the character unless the question asks you to.
points: **How it ends.** Four sentences is plenty.

question.text: What does Don Quixote blame after the windmills?
options: The enchanter Freston, for changing the giants
question.explain: Never 'I was wrong'. Always 'somebody changed them to spite me'.

cards.title: Proofread backwards
cards.text: Reading your own writing forwards, you see what you meant. Read the last sentence first and you see what you wrote.
points: **Two minutes** at the end of the paper.

question.text: An apostrophe can be used to make a word plural.
question.explain: Never. It marks possession or a missing letter. This is the single most common error in the topic.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **Find the subject**, ignore the phrase between.

quiz.text: What is the plural of 'key'?
quiz.explain: Week 1. The -ies rule applies only after a consonant. Vowel plus y takes a plain -s.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: What is the plural of 'roof'?
quiz.explain: Week 1. Many f words become -ves, but roofs, chiefs and beliefs do not.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: Which is correct?
options: There were fewer cars on the road.
There were less cars on the road.
There were fewer traffic on the road.
There were less car on the road.
quiz.explain: Week 2. Fewer is for things you count; less is for things you measure.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: Which is the correct plural possessive?
quiz.explain: Week 3. The plural already ends in s, so it takes the apostrophe only.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: What is the plural possessive of 'child'?
quiz.explain: Week 3. The plural does not end in s, so it takes apostrophe then s.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: Which sentence uses it's correctly?
quiz.explain: Week 3. It's always means it is or it has. Expand it to check.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: Which word is a possessive pronoun rather than a determiner?
quiz.explain: Week 4. A pronoun stands alone; a determiner sits in front of a noun.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: Possessive pronouns like yours and theirs take an apostrophe.
quiz.explain: Week 4. They are already possessive, so no apostrophe is ever needed.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: Which is correct?
options: Everyone has his or her own locker.
quiz.explain: Week 5. Everyone is grammatically singular, along with each, either and neither.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: How many compound personal pronouns are there?
quiz.explain: Week 6. The same eight words serve as both reflexive and intensive pronouns.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: Which of these is not a word?
quiz.explain: Week 6. Hisself and theirselves are not informal forms. They are not words at all.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: In 'She fixed the bike herself', what is 'herself' doing?
options: Adding emphasis; the sentence works without it
Acting as the object of the verb
quiz.explain: Week 7. Delete it and the sentence still works, so it is intensive rather than reflexive.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: Which is correct?
options: He do not likes the rain.
quiz.explain: Week 8. Does already carries the ending, so the main verb stays plain.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: Which verbs change in the simple present tense?
quiz.explain: Week 8. Third person singular is the only form that takes -s or -es.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: Which is correct?
options: Neither the coach nor the players were ready.
Neither the coach nor the players was ready.
Neither the coach nor the players is ready.
Neither the coach nor the players has ready.
quiz.explain: Week 9. With or and nor, the verb matches whichever subject is nearer. Players is nearer.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: Which is correct?
options: Mathematics have been his best subjects.
quiz.explain: Week 10. News, mathematics and physics all end in -s and are singular.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: Which is correct?
options: A number of students are waiting.
A number of students is waiting.
The number of students are waiting.
A number of student is waiting.
quiz.explain: Week 10. 'A number of' takes a plural verb; 'the number of' takes a singular one.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: In 'There are three books on the shelf', 'there' is the subject.
quiz.explain: Week 9. 'There' is never the subject. Books is, and it follows the verb.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten English topics of the term

quiz.text: What makes Don Quixote set out as a knight?
options: He has read so many books about knights that he believes them
He is ordered to by a king
He is running from the law
He inherits a suit of armour
quiz.explain: Chapter 1. A quiet gentleman, a skinny horse and a wall of books about chivalry.
quiz.objective: Recall the episodes of Don Quixote covered this term

quiz.text: What happens to Andrés, the boy tied to the tree?
options: The farmer beats him harder once Don Quixote has gone
He is freed and paid his wages
He runs away to the city
quiz.explain: Chapter 3. The rescue leaves him worse off than if nobody had come at all.
quiz.objective: Recall the episodes of Don Quixote covered this term

quiz.text: What do the priest and the barber do in the library?
options: Judge the books one by one and burn most of them
Lock the books away and say nothing
quiz.explain: Chapter 5. The priest argues for particular books and saves them, which is the joke.
quiz.objective: Recall the episodes of Don Quixote covered this term

quiz.text: What is Sancho Panza promised?
quiz.explain: Chapter 6. He is practical and sceptical about knights, but he believes this.
quiz.objective: Recall the episodes of Don Quixote covered this term

quiz.text: What is the golden helmet of Mambrino actually?
quiz.explain: The barber is wearing it upside down in the rain to keep his hat dry.
quiz.objective: Recall the episodes of Don Quixote covered this term

quiz.text: What does Don Quixote charge at, believing it to be two armies?
quiz.explain: The shepherds bring him down with stones from their slings, and he blames the enchanter again.
quiz.objective: Recall the episodes of Don Quixote covered this term

teacher.summary: Week 11 is exam week for English and covers both strands. The grammar half of the deck is reduced to the three tests that carry the most marks: expand it's to check the apostrophe, delete the -self word to tell reflexive from intensive, and cross out the phrase between subject and verb before choosing agreement. The novel half names the pattern that runs through every chapter — the enchanter excuse — and turns it into a transferable question: what would disprove this? That is worth more than the plot recall, though the paper tests both. Every Don Quixote detail in the quiz was checked against the lesson it came from.
discussion: Ask him to expand every it's and who's he writes for a week. The error disappears fast.
Ask him to delete the -self word from three sentences and say which ones break.
Ask what the enchanter excuse lets Don Quixote avoid, every single time.
Ask what would have to happen for Don Quixote to admit he was wrong. Nothing would, and that is the point.
teacher.extension: Have him retell one episode in exactly four sentences: who, what he believes, what actually happens, how it ends. Four is the constraint that makes it a skill.
misconceptions: 'An apostrophe can make a plural.' Never. It marks possession or a missing letter.
'The verb agrees with the closest noun.' It agrees with the subject, which is often not the closest.
'Any word ending in -self is reflexive.' Only if it is the object. Delete it and see.
'Don Quixote is simply stupid.' He decides what things mean in advance, which is a different problem.
